readmeHtml.0xnirmata.github.io:
Portfolio

0xNirmata's personal portfolio — a terminal-styled, GitHub-centered site: black background, monospace, no gradients, no frameworks fighting the aesthetic. Built with Astro as a fully static site (no server, no database) so it can be hosted for free and stays fast by default.

The content is data-driven: every project on the site is a Markdown file with structured frontmatter (see Adding a project), so adding, reordering, or archiving one never touches page code.

Stack

  • Astro (static output) + TypeScript (strict).
  • Content Collections (astro:content, glob loader) with a Zod schema for validation — a malformed project file fails astro check / astro build instead of silently rendering wrong.
  • Plain CSS (src/styles/terminal.css) — the whole visual system lives in one file via custom properties (:root { --background, --foreground, ... }). No CSS framework, no client-side JS beyond what Astro needs for nothing (this site ships essentially zero JS).

Structure

src/
├── components/          Header, Footer, ProjectEntry
├── content/projects/    one Markdown file per project (the actual content)
├── content.config.ts    the projects collection schema (Zod)
├── data/site.ts         global config: identity, GitHub link, profile copy —
│                        the single source of truth for text repeated across pages
├── layouts/             TerminalLayout.astro (SEO tags, header/footer wrap)
├── pages/                index, projects/, projects/[id], about, 404
└── styles/terminal.css   the whole visual system (CSS custom properties)

Commands

Purpose Command Notes
Install npm install requires Node ≥22.12
Dev server npm run dev serves localhost:4321 with hot reload
Type check npx astro check validates content frontmatter against the Zod schema too
Build npm run build outputs the static site to dist/
Preview build npm run preview serves the production build from dist/ locally

There is no test suite and no linter configured — this is a static content site; correctness is astro check (types + content schema) and astro build (every route actually generates) passing.

Adding a project

  1. Create src/content/projects/<slug>.md. The filename becomes the URL slug (/projects/<slug>).
  2. Fill in the frontmatter — see any existing file for the shape, enforced by the schema in src/content.config.ts:
    • title, description, status (active | maintained | experimental | completed | archived), year, featured, order, technologies.
    • github — leave "" if the repo isn't public yet; the page shows [private / on request] instead of a broken link.
    • Optional: demo, documentation, problem, solution.
  3. Write the body in Markdown — this becomes the project's full write-up.
  4. npm run build to confirm it compiles, then commit.

order is a deliberate ranking (interdependent projects grouped and kept in their real appearance order, groups ranked by relevance) — not chronological or alphabetical. Keep that in mind when inserting a new project rather than just appending it at the end. featured: true projects also appear on the homepage, in order.

Deployment — GitHub Pages (free)

This site is 100% static, so GitHub Pages hosts it for free with no separate account needed beyond GitHub itself. Two things decide the URL shape:

  • Repo named <your-username>.github.io → the site is served at the root: https://<your-username>.github.io. No extra config needed.
  • Repo with any other name (e.g. portfolio) → the site is served at https://<your-username>.github.io/<repo-name>. Astro needs to know that path prefix or every internal link and asset will 404.

1. Push the repo to GitHub

git remote add origin https://github.com/<your-username>/<repo-name>.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

(gh repo create <repo-name> --public --source=. --push does the same in one step if you use the GitHub CLI.)

2. If the repo is not <username>.github.io, set base

In astro.config.mjs:

// @ts-check
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
	site: 'https://<your-username>.github.io',
	base: '/<repo-name>', // omit entirely if the repo IS <username>.github.io
});

Setting site (regardless of which case you're in) also turns the canonical URL and Open Graph tags in TerminalLayout.astro back on — they're currently skipped because no production domain is configured yet.

3. Add the deploy workflow

Create .github/workflows/deploy.yml:

name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: withastro/action@v3
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

withastro/action installs dependencies, runs astro check + astro build, and uploads dist/ as the Pages artifact in one step.

4. Turn on Pages

In the GitHub repo: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions. Push to main (or re-run the workflow) and the site goes live at the URL from step 2 a couple of minutes later — GitHub shows the exact URL and deploy status on the same Settings → Pages screen.

Custom domain later (optional)

Settings → Pages → Custom domain, then point the domain's DNS at GitHub Pages (ALIAS/ANAME or A records to GitHub's IPs for an apex domain, CNAME for a subdomain — GitHub's UI shows the exact records once you type the domain). Update site in astro.config.mjs to the new domain and drop base.

Other free static hosts

If GitHub Pages ever feels limiting (e.g. you want image optimisation, edge functions, or SSR later), this same repo deploys to Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or Vercel with no code changes — connect the GitHub repo in any of their dashboards, build command npm run build, output directory dist. All three have a free tier and none need the base path GitHub Pages project sites require.

Before deploying — checklist

  • Set site (and base if applicable) in astro.config.mjs.
  • Re-check that every project's github field still resolves — repo visibility can change (gh repo list <username> to check).
  • npm run build locally once more; commit package-lock.json if it changed.

Documentation complète du projet, organisée pour reprendre le travail après une pause prolongée.

🗺️ Plan de lecture conseillé

Si tu reprends le projet maintenant, lis dans cet ordre :

  2. 02_ROADMAP.md Plan détaillé de ce qui reste à coder, étape par étape, avec dépendances claires.

  7. tests/02_TESTS_PARSER.md Liste complète des tests Parser, organisée par phase d'implémentation (~80 tests).

docs/
├── README.md                          ← ce fichier

    ├── 00_STRATEGIE.md                ← stratégie de tests + doctest

03_TESTS_AVANCES.md à créer plus tard (semantic + codegen).

  • Lexer : ✅ fonctionnel, aucun test unitaire.
  • Parser : ⚠️ 15% squelette, classes manquantes, bugs de types (enum keyword n'existe pas), méthode parse() qui ne lance jamais parseProgram().

Prochaine action :

  1. Mettre en place doctest (voir tests/04_INTEGRATION_CMAKE.md).
  2. Écrire les tests Lexer (voir tests/01_TESTS_LEXER.md).
  3. Refactor Parser.hpp (voir 02_ROADMAP.md étape A).

Quand tu avances dans le projet, mets à jour :

readmeHtml.Minishell:
Minishell

Implémentation d'un shell minimaliste en langage C.

📋 Table des matières

  • Fonctionnalités
  • Compilation
  • Utilisation
  • Structure du projet
  • Corrections appliquées
  • Tests

🚀 Fonctionnalités

Built-in commands (obligatoires)

Commande Description Arguments
echo Affiche des arguments avec options -n pour sauter le newline final -[n] [string...]
cd Change de répertoire de travail [chemin]
pwd Affiche le répertoire de travail absolu actuel -
env Affiche toutes les variables d'environnement triées -
export Affiche ou ajoute une variable d'environnement [var=val]
unset Supprime une variable d'environnement [variable]
exit Quitte le shell avec un code de sortie [code]

Fonctionnalités principales

  • ✅ Parsing et tokenisation des commandes (gestion des quotes ", ')
  • ✅ Expansion des variables environmentales $VAR, $$, $?
  • ✅ Redirections d'entrées/sorties (>, >>, <, <<)
  • ✅ Here-documents avec littéraux et expansions de variables
  • ✅ Chaînes de commandes via pipes |
  • ✅ Gestion des signaux (CTRL+C, CTRL+D)
  • ✅ Variables spéciales: $? (dernier code), $$ (PID shell)
  • ✅ Variables d'environnement PWD/OLDPWD mises à jour dynamiquement

🔨 Compilation

# Nettoyer et compiler le projet
make clean && make

# Résultat: exécutable 'minishell'

Dépendances

  • libft - Bibliothèque utilitaire (doit être placée dans dossier libft)
  • Compilateur C standard avec support POSIX

💻 Utilisation

./minishell

Exemples:

Commandes simples:

$ echo "Hello World"
Hello World

$ pwd
/home/user

$ cd /tmp && pwd
/tmp

Variables et expansion:

$ export MONVAR=valeur
$ echo $MONVAR
valeur

$ $$            # Affiche le PID du shell
12345

$ exit 42       # Quitte avec code 42

Redirections:

# Sortie vers fichier
$ echo "test" > output.txt

# Redirection append
$ echo "ajout" >> output.txt

# Entrée depuis fichier  
$ cat < input.txt

# Here-document
$ cat << EOF
content
more content
EOF

Pipes:

$ echo "hello" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'
HELLO

$ env | grep PATH | cut -d: -f1

Combinaisons complexes:

export VAR=test && echo $VAR > tmp.txt && cat tmp.txt << EOF
bonus
EOF

📁 Structure du projet

Minishell/
├── includes/
│   └── minishell.h           # Headers globaux et structures
├── libft/                    # LibFT (à fournir)
├── src/
│   ├── main.c               # Entry point
│   ├── minishell.c          # Boucle principale du shell
│   │
│   ├── parsing/             # Analyse syntaxique
│   │   ├── parsing/         # Parsing des commandes
│   │   ├── tokenize/        # Tokenisation (quotes, operators)
│   │   ├── expand/          # Expansion variables $VAR, $$, $?
│   │   ├── commands/        # Construction de l'arbre de commandes
│   │   └── utils/           # Utils parsing
│   │
│   ├── execution/           # Exécution
│   │   ├── executions_utils/# Gestion forks/pipes/sigs
│   │   ├── redirect/        # Redirections fichier, here-doc
│   │   └── here_docs/       # Traitement here-documents
│   │
│   ├── builtins/            # Commandes intégrées
│   │   ├── cd/              # Changement directory
│   │   ├── env/             # Variables environnement
│   │   ├── export/          # Affichage/ajout variables
│   │   ├── exit/            # Sortie shell
│   │   ├── echo/            # Affichage arguments
│   │   ├── pwd/             # Directory actuel
│   │   └── unset/           # Suppression variables
│   │
│   ├── free/                # Nettoyage mémoire
│   ├── signals/             # Gestion CTRL+C/D
│   └── debug/               # Debug (optionnel)
│
├── Makefile                 # Construction projet complet  
└── README.md               # Cette documentation

✅ Corrections Appliquées (Version Finale)

Le code initial contenait plusieurs bugs identifiés. Voici les 7 corrections critiques applicées:

1. 🔧 Double Free Corrigé

  • Fichier: src/parsing/parsing.c : Ligne 42
  • Problème: free(shell->token) après ft_lstclear_cust()
  • Fix: Suppression de la ligne double free qui causait segfaults

2. 🔧 Unset Always Returns ecode=0

  • Fichier: src/builtins/unset.c : Ligne 51 (ajoutée)
  • Problème: Missing return; → ecode écrasé à 1 systématiquement!
  • Fix: Ajout de return; après shell->ecode = 0;

3. 🔧 CD Sets PWD Correctement

  • Fichier: src/builtins/cd.c : Lignes 60, 68-70
  • Problème: Utilisation de chemin utilisateur non-résolu ("path")
  • Fix: getcwd(newpwd, 4096) puis update_pwd(shell, newpwd, 0);

4. 🔧 Rebuild_str Ne Perd Pas Données

  • Fichier: src/parsing/commands/utils2.c : Lignes 21-32
  • Problème: ft_strjoin(NULL, tab[0]) ne retourne pas le premier élément!
  • Fix: Init avec tmp = ft_strdup("") et fonction strjoin_free()

5. 🔧 Exit Sort Proprement

  • Fichier: src/builtins/exit.c : Lignes 39-43
  • Problème: Juste printf() sans free_all() et `exit()→shell continue!
  • Fix: Ajout de: 
    printf("exit: too many arguments\n");
free_all(shell, NULL, 1);
exit(1);

6. 🔧 ASCII Art Supprimé

  • Fichier: src/main.c : Lignes 19-40 (35 lignes supprimées)
  • Problème: Code superflu polluant stdout
  • Fix: main() simplifié à seulement: 
    minishell(env);
return (0);

7. 🔧 Stat Check Correct File

  • Fichier: src/execution/redirect/files_manager.c : Lignes 47, 21
  • Problème: stat(program, &statbuf) check le mauvais fichier!
  • Fix: stat(full_path, &statbuf) pour vérifier le chemin complet

🧪 Tests Recommandés

Voici une liste de tests pour valider les corrections:

#!/bin/bash
# test_minishell.sh - Tests complets des corrections

echo "=== TEST 1: Unset ecode ==="
./minishell <<< 'export TEST=hello && unset TEST && echo "UNSET WORKS"'
# ✅ Devrait afficher "UNSET WORKS" (ecode=0 après unset)

echo "=== TEST 2: cd + PWD canonic ==="  
./minishell -c 'cd /var/../tmp && pwd'
# ✅ Devrait afficher "/tmp" pas "/var/../tmp"

echo "=== TEST 3: Exit trop d'arguments ==="
echo 'exit arg1 arg2 arg3' | ./minishell
# ✅ Message + shell QUITTE IMMEDIATEMENT (code 1)

echo "=== TEST 4: rebuild_str expansion ==="
./minishell <<< '$HOME'
# ✅ Devrait afficher le chemin complet du home

echo "=== TEST 5: Double free avoided ==="
./minishell <<< 'cd /tmp; export A=1; unset A; cd ~; exit'
# ✅ Aucun segfault (le double free se déclenche après parsing complexe)

echo "=== TEST 6: Clean startup ===" 
./minishell <<< 'exit' | head -3
# ✅ Seulement: minishell->, pas d'ASCII art!

echo "=== ALL TESTS PASSED ==="

Résulats attendus après corrections:

Test Sans correction Avec correction
Unset && cmd ❌ ecode=1 break && ✅ Cmd s'exécute
cd /a/../b pwd ❌ /a/../b path raw ✅ /b canonique
exit arg1 arg2(arg3) ⚠️ Continue après msg ✅ Shell quitte (exit 1)
Expansion $VAR 🔴 Données perdues possible ✅ Expansion complète
Segfault parsing 🟡 Possible sur certains cas ✅ Memory safe
ASCII art start ⚠️ 35 lignes stdout ✅ Clean prompt

🎓 Notes

  • Toutes les fonctionnalités obligatoires implémentées
  • Gestion robuste des erreurs et allocations mémoire
  • Code conforme aux standards POSIX pour Linux
  • Compatible bash dans la majorité des cas d'usage

Version finale: Code corrigé et stable ✅
Date dernière mise à jour: Août 2025
Statut prêt pour production: OUI ✓
readmeHtml.IoT:
🎓 Inception of Things

📋 Introduction

Inception of Things (IoT) is a project designed to provide hands-on experience with Kubernetes, container orchestration, and DevOps practices. This project serves as an excellent introduction to the complex world of Kubernetes by utilizing lightweight alternatives like K3s and k3d.

🎯 Project Goals

  • ✅ Set up a Kubernetes cluster using K3s on virtual machines (Vagrant)
  • ✅ Deploy multiple applications with different replicas
  • ✅ Configure Ingress for managing external access
  • ✅ Use k3d to run Kubernetes clusters inside Docker containers
  • ✅ Implement GitOps with ArgoCD and GitLab CI/CD pipeline
  • ✅ Understand the fundamentals of container orchestration

📁 Repository Structure

IoT/
├── README.md                    # This file
├── .gitignore
├── p1/                          # Part 1: K3s Cluster with Vagrant
│   ├── Vagrantfile             # VM configuration (server + worker nodes)
│   └── scripts/
│       ├── server.sh           # Master node K3s installation script
│       └── worker.sh           # Worker node joining script
├── p2/                          # Part 2: Deploy Applications
│   ├── Vagrantfile             # Single VM with K3s
│   ├── confs/                  # Kubernetes manifests
│   │   ├── app1.yaml          # Deployment + Service for app1 (1 replica)
│   │   ├── app2.yaml          # Deployment + Service for app2 (3 replicas)
│   │   ├── app3.yaml          # Deployment + Service for app3 (1 replica)
│   │   └── ingress.yaml       # Ingress routing configuration
│   └── scripts/
│       └── setup.sh            # K3s + applications deployment script
├── p3/                          # Part 3: k3d Cluster Creation
│   ├── confs/                  # Kubernetes manifests for playground app
│   │   ├── deploy.yaml        # Deployment configuration
│   │   ├── service.yaml       # Service definition
│   │   └── ingress.yaml       # Ingress for playground
│   └── scripts/
│       └── install.sh          # Docker, k3d, kubectl installation script
└── bonus/                       # Bonus: GitLab + ArgoCD GitOps
    ├── confs/
    │   ├── gitlab-values.yaml     # Helm values for GitLab CE
    │   ├── argocd-gitlab-app.yaml # ArgoCD Application definition
    │   └── namespace.yaml         # GitLab namespace creation
    └── scripts/
        └── install-gitlab.sh      # Full GitLab + ArgoCD setup script

🛠️ Prerequisites

Software Requirements

Tool Minimum Version Purpose
Vagrant 2.2+ VM management
VirtualBox 6.0+ Hypervisor for nested virtualization
Docker 20.10+ Container runtime (for k3d)
kubectl 1.25+ Kubernetes CLI
k3d 5.0+ K3s in Docker cluster tool
Helm 3.8+ Package manager for Kubernetes (Bonus)

Hardware Requirements

  • RAM: Minimum 8GB recommended (16GB preferred for GitLab bonus)
  • CPU: 4+ cores with virtualization support (VT-x/AMD-V)
  • Disk: At least 20GB free space

Enable Nested Virtualization (for VirtualBox)

# For better performance on Windows/Mac, enable nested virtualization:
VBoxManage modifyvm "your-vm-name" --nested-hw-virt on

📚 Project Parts

Part 1: K3s Cluster with Vagrant

Objective: Create a two-node Kubernetes cluster (master + worker) using Vagrant and K3s.

Architecture
┌─────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────┐
│   Server Node   │◄────────►│   Worker Node   │
│   (Master)      │  k3s     │   (Agent)       │
│   192.168.x.110 │ cluster  │   192.168.x.111 │
└─────────────────┘          └─────────────────┘
        │                          │
        └──────────┬───────────────┘
                   ▼
          Kubernetes cluster
Features
  • Master Node (0xnirmataS): K3s server with control plane
  • Worker Node (0xnirmataSW): K3s agent node joining the cluster
  • Token Sharing: Automatic token passing via shared /vagrant folder
  • Network Interface Detection: Automatic flannel interface configuration
How to Run
cd p1
vagrant up

What happens:

  1. Vagrant provisions two Debian Bookworm VMs
  2. Server script installs K3s master node
  3. Worker script waits for token, then joins as agent
  4. Both nodes form a functional Kubernetes cluster

Part 2: Deploy Applications with Ingress

Objective: Deploy three applications with different configurations and expose them via Ingress.

Architecture
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│  app1    │    │  app2    │    │  app3    │
│ (1 repl) │    │ (3 repl) │    │ (1 repl) │
└────┬─────┘    └────┬─────┘    └────┬─────┘
     │               │               │
     ▼               ▼               ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Ingress Controller             │
│                                             │
│  app1.com → app1                            │
│  app2.com → app2                            │
│  /        → app3                            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Deployed Applications
App Replicas Image Host/Path
app1 1 traefik/whoami app1.com
app2 3 traefik/whoami app2.com
app3 1 traefik/whoami / (default)
How to Run
cd p2
vagrant up

After provisioning, verify deployment:

vagrant ssh 0xnirmataS
kubectl get all --all-namespaces
kubectl get ingress

Part 3: k3d Cluster Creation

Objective: Create a K3s cluster running inside Docker containers using k3d.

Why k3d?

Instead of heavy VMs, k3d uses Docker containers as Kubernetes nodes, making it:

  • ⚡ Faster startup (seconds vs minutes)
  • 💾 Less resource-intensive
  • 🔄 More portable and reproducible
Architecture
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Docker Host               │
│                                     │
│  ┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────┐   │
│  │  k3d server  │──►│ loadbal  │   │
│  └──────────────┘   └────┬─────┘   │
│                          │         │
│  Port Mapping:           │         │
│  8080:80 (traefik)       │         │
│  8888:8888 (playground)  │         │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
Deployed Application
  • Image: rmarcas42/playground:v1
  • Port: 8888 → accessible at http://localhost:8888
  • Namespace: dev
How to Run
cd p3
bash scripts/install.sh

This script:

  1. Installs Docker
  2. Installs k3d (v5.6.0)
  3. Installs kubectl
  4. Creates iot-cluster with port mappings
  5. Applies Kubernetes manifests from confs/

Bonus: GitLab + ArgoCD GitOps

Objective: Implement a complete GitOps pipeline using GitLab CE and ArgoCD.

Architecture
┌─────────────┐      ┌─────────────┐      ┌─────────────┐
│   GitLab    │────►│  ArgoCD     │────►│   k3d       │
│ CI/CD Repo  │  sync│ Controller  │deploy│ Cluster     │
│ (IaC Config)│      │             │      │ Playground  │
└─────────────┘      └─────────────┘      └─────────────┘
Components Installed
  • GitLab CE: Lightweight GitLab Edition with optimized resource requests
    • Redis: 256Mi memory
    • PostgreSQL: 256Mi memory
    • Webservice: 512Mi memory
  • ArgoCD: GitOps continuous delivery tool
  • nginx-ingress: For GitLab traffic routing
Port Mappings
Port Service URL
8080 LoadBalancer (traefik) http://localhost:8080
8888 Playground app http://localhost:8888
8929 GitLab (HTTP) http://127.0.0.1.nip.io
How to Run
cd bonus
bash scripts/install-gitlab.sh

⏰ Note: This takes 5-10 minutes as it installs many components.

Access GitLab

After installation:

  1. Visit http://127.0.0.1.nip.io (or http://localhost:8929)
  2. Login with admin credentials (stored in ArgoCD or generated by GitLab)
GitOps Flow
# argocd-gitlab-app.yaml defines:
sourceRepo: gitlab/playground.git (contains deploy.yaml, service.yaml, ingress.yaml)
destination: k3d cluster (automatically syncs changes)
syncPolicy: 
  - selfHeal: true  (auto-rollback drift)
  - prune: true     (delete untracked resources)

🔧 Configuration Details

Network Configuration (P1 & P2)

Node IP Address Hostname Role

readmeHtml.ft_ping:
🛰️ ft_ping

A from-scratch reimplementation of the classic ping utility in C

Reference implementation: inetutils-2.0

📖 About

ft_ping is a reimplementation of the Unix ping command, a network diagnostic tool used to test reachability of a host on an IP network and measure the round-trip time of packets sent to that host.

Under the hood, it crafts ICMP Echo Request packets, sends them through a raw socket, and listens for the matching ICMP Echo Reply messages — computing the elapsed time with microsecond precision.

This project was built strictly from scratch: no calls to the system ping, no reuse of an existing implementation's source.

✨ Features

Mandatory

  • ✅ IPv4 and FQDN targets
  • ✅ -v verbose mode (prints anomalous ICMP packets without exiting)
  • ✅ -? usage screen
  • ✅ Output formatting matches inetutils-2.0
  • ✅ Clean statistics on SIGINT (packets sent/received, loss %, RTT min/avg/max/stddev)
  • ✅ Robust error handling — no segfaults, no leaks

Bonus (planned / in progress)

Flag Description
-s Payload size
-w Global deadline
-W Per-packet timeout
-n No DNS resolution
-l Preload
-f Flood mode
-p Custom fill pattern
--ttl Custom TTL
… more to come

🔧 Build

Requirements

  • A Linux environment (kernel > 3.14, Debian-like recommended)
  • gcc or clang
  • make

Build targets

make           # Build the project
make re        # Full rebuild
make clean     # Remove object files
make fclean    # Remove objects + binary
make debug     # Build with -g3, AddressSanitizer & UBSan
make setcap    # Grant CAP_NET_RAW (run without sudo)
make help      # Show available targets

The build system auto-detects every .c file under src/ (recursively) and uses -MMD -MP to regenerate object files whenever a header changes.

🚀 Usage

ping requires raw-socket privileges. Pick one of:

# Option 1 — run as root
sudo ./ft_ping google.com

# Option 2 — one-time capability grant, then run as regular user
make setcap
./ft_ping google.com

Basic examples

./ft_ping 8.8.8.8
./ft_ping google.com
./ft_ping -v example.org
./ft_ping -?

Sample output

PING google.com (142.250.74.238): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 142.250.74.238: icmp_seq=0 ttl=116 time=12.345 ms
64 bytes from 142.250.74.238: icmp_seq=1 ttl=116 time=11.987 ms
64 bytes from 142.250.74.238: icmp_seq=2 ttl=116 time=12.104 ms
^C
--- google.com ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 3 packets received, 0% packet loss
round-trip min/avg/max/stddev = 11.987/12.145/12.345/0.148 ms

🗂️ Project structure

ft_ping/
├── Makefile
├── README.md
├── include/
│   └── ft_ping.h        # Public headers
├── src/
│   ├── main.c           # Entry point, argument parsing
│   ├── socket/          # Raw socket setup
│   ├── packet/          # ICMP packet crafting, checksum
│   ├── loop/            # Send/receive loop, signal handling
│   ├── stats/           # RTT statistics, final summary
│   └── utils/           # Misc helpers (error, dns, time)
└── build/               # Auto-generated object & dep files

(Structure indicative — to be adapted as the project grows.)

🧠 Technical notes

  • Raw sockets — created with socket(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_ICMP). This bypasses the kernel's transport layer and requires elevated privileges.
  • ICMP checksum — standard 16-bit one's-complement sum, computed over the ICMP header + payload only (the kernel fills in the IP header).
  • Packet identification — we tag outgoing packets with getpid() & 0xFFFF to filter incoming replies destined to us.
  • Timing — high-resolution timestamps via clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, …) to avoid artifacts from wall-clock adjustments (NTP, DST).
  • Signals — SIGINT triggers graceful shutdown + final statistics; SIGALRM (via setitimer) paces packet emission at 1 Hz.
  • No reverse DNS on received packets — the target is resolved once at startup via getaddrinfo, then the raw IP is displayed for replies.

⚠️ Constraints (from the subject)

  • 🚫 Calling the system ping (directly or via fork/exec) is forbidden.
  • 🚫 Reusing the source code of an existing ping implementation is forbidden.
  • ✅ The entire libc is allowed.
  • ✅ The printf family is allowed (no need to reimplement it).
  • ✅ Reception tolerance of ±30 ms is accepted.

📚 References

  • RFC 792 — Internet Control Message Protocol
  • RFC 1122 — Requirements for Internet Hosts
  • inetutils-2.0 source — reference implementation
  • man 7 raw, man 7 icmp, man 2 socket, man 3 getaddrinfo

Built with care.
